audit.whatIsWrong: Level-chart stages carried a closing verdict that contradicted the stage owner (for example a stage marked Jayce ending "Camille is favoured here").
audit.why: The full-layer phase text was templated; the tail sentence was never reconciled with phases[].side, so the written verdict and the chart disagreed on the same page.
audit.corrected: Each phase why now closes with the verdict that matches its own side field, so early / mid / side-lane ownership reads consistently.

audit.why: Spike stages line up with the real kits: Camille at 2 (Hookshot, 16s at rank 1), 6 (The Hextech Ultimatum, 140s at rank 1) and her Sheen item; Jayce at Mercury Cannon/Mercury Hammer (6).

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 stage told you to "use the cast's brief untargetable frame" on The Hextech Ultimatum to dodge Jayce's key spell.
audit.why: Riot's own description of The Hextech Ultimatum is "Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area" — there is no untargetable window. The kit file's untargetable/channel flags on R are tooltip-parse misfires and contradict the description.
audit.corrected: The stage now says the dash grants no immunity and keys R to being spent after the enemy spell rather than into it.

edits.before: Short shield-window trades. Start W (Tactical Sweep) for the outer-edge poke and heal, or Q for the empowered auto into a melee threat. Do not extend past your Adaptive Defenses shield or your raw HP falls behind. Jayce is favoured here.
edits.after: Short shield-window trades. Start W (Tactical Sweep) for the outer-edge poke and heal, or Q for the empowered auto into a melee threat. Do not extend past your Adaptive Defenses shield or your raw HP falls behind. This is a clean skill phase.

edits.before: The Hextech Ultimatum (R) isolates a target in a 1v1 they cannot leave. Use the cast's brief untargetable frame to dodge Jayce's Shock Blast or burst, then focus the trapped target. Jayce is favoured here.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum (R) isolates a target in a 1v1 they cannot leave. The dash grants no immunity, so spend R once Jayce's Shock Blast is gone, not into it, then focus the trapped target. This is a clean skill phase.

edits.before: Trinity Force / Sheen turns your Q resets lethal and your wall dives become kill threats. Start applying deep side-lane pressure and clearing camps between waves. This is a clean skill phase.
edits.after: Trinity Force / Sheen turns your Q resets lethal and your wall dives become kill threats. Start applying deep side-lane pressure and clearing camps between waves. Jayce is favoured here.

edits.before: This is where you take over. Once you can E-in, W-slow and land both Q hits, his poke can't out-damage your burst, and the move speed off Q's recast keeps you glued to him. Everything Jayce has is built to keep you ranged — cannon poke, the hammer-E knockback, the gate — so make him whiff the knockback and you win the trade every time. Time your Adaptive Defense shield to swallow his burst combo before you dive. At 6 your Hextech Ultimatum is the trump card: lock him in the arena and he can't kite, gate, or knock you out, so W-heal off him and delete him in the isolated 1v1.

notes: Camille kit file flags R as channel/interruptible and untargetable; both contradict Riot's own description (a dash plus an anchoring zone) and were treated as tooltip-parse misfires, per the kit README. Packet win rate 53.57% over 659 games.
